title: Claude, the blind judge of every past decision and experiment, every judgment kept whole
request: The owner: 'go ahead with Claude as the judge of all process and procedure that help us collect data, also from past decisions and past experiments'; 'record and store all these judgements with all details; save all permanently'; 'do not truncate: run first, record and store, then save all data permanently, then truncate'.
plan: Reuse the blind labeler (decision_labeler) rather than build a judge: it never shows DCLab's answer and may say it cannot tell.
Measure the judge on homework with known truth before trusting it.
Judge every real past decision (the live sessions, the twin lanes, the development workspace) and harvest the verdicts as silver, weighted by the measured accuracy.
Review the past experiments with the campaign's own reviewer, beside the earlier one.
Keep every judgment whole before anything is cut; archive the live runs permanently.

decisions.decision: The judge is the existing blind labeler, extended (every decision, any ledger, in parallel).
decisions.why: The owner's rule: enhance, never replace; it already keeps model labels apart from people's and the truth.

decisions.decision: Silver weights by point and confidence, from the latest judge run on homework; usable at 0.8 and above.
decisions.why: Claude's high-confidence verdicts were right 166 of 166 while its low ones were near chance on some points: one weight per point would throw away the good half or keep the bad.

decisions.decision: A verdict on a decision Claude itself made is kept but never usable.
Every judgment is written whole (sent, raw reply, tokens, seconds, cost) before the ledger's short copy.
decisions.why: The owner's rule after 425 of 725 reasons had been cut before anything kept them.

decisions.decision: Experiment reviews run beside the campaign's reviewer and never write the result files.
decisions.why: Rule 3: results are never edited; the earlier reviews stay as they were.

decisions.decision: A model that refuses a sampling option is retried once without it and never sent it again.
decisions.why: Sonnet 5.5 refuses temperature; the product's model must not fail a caller for it.

change: ledger/model_labels.py (every, ledger, workers, judgments kept whole); students_exam.py (judge mode, homework as a ledger, judged, keep_verdicts with the full reply, Whole for the exam's replies); lake/harvest.py (the judge's silver view, weights by point and confidence, self-judged kept apart); llm_review.py and cli.py (beside, cap); models/anthropic_client.py (sampling refused: retry once, remember); archive.py (live tests and the image sets archived); tests in five files.

findings.defect: 425 of 725 judge reasons were cut to 180 characters before anything kept them whole.
findings.scenario: SEX-003's verdicts: the ledger's evidence field is short, and only the cut copy was written.
findings.cause: The labeler wrote the contract's short reason and nothing else.
findings.fix: Every judgment is written whole to judgments.jsonl before the short copy; the homework was judged again (SEX-004) with every reply kept.

findings.defect: Claude refused every experiment review: temperature is deprecated for Sonnet 5.5.
findings.scenario: The campaign reviewer sends temperature=0.2; every request was a 400 with no tokens spent.
findings.cause: The adapter passed sampling options through to a model that refuses them.
findings.fix: A 400 refusing temperature or top_p is retried once without them and the model is remembered.

findings.defect: One review was cut by the reply's length limit.
findings.scenario: EXP-023: the reply stopped at its limit (8,607 characters) and could not be parsed.
findings.cause: The reviewer leaves the limit to the adapter's default.
findings.fix: Its raw reply is kept whole; a re-ask with a larger limit is left open.

findings.defect: Test fixtures used ledger ids shorter than the contract allows and decisions the ledger refuses.
findings.scenario: 'r0' ids; a model's answer used at level 0.
findings.cause: Fixtures written without the contract's rules.
findings.fix: Fixtures use valid ids and a Claude-led decision at level 2 with the rule's answer beside it.

measurements.name: the blind judge on homework (SEX-003, SEX-004)
measurements.gate: none fixed: the judge's accuracy per point and per confidence, the basis of the silver weights
measurements.result: 820 decisions each run, EUR 1.88 and 1.85; judged 722 to 725, unsure 95 to 98; accuracy 0.95 to 0.96 category code, 0.96 to 0.97 group, 1.0 flip, 0.93 wrong image label, 0.80 to 0.82 identifier, near copy and role, about 0.49 time and 0.52 leakage; high-confidence verdicts right 166 of 166 in both runs
measurements.against_gate: Not scored: a measurement of the judge, reproduced by a second run.
limits: Homework weighted to the hard cases (disagreements first).

measurements.name: the judge on every real past decision
measurements.gate: none fixed: silver labels, weighted by the homework measurement
measurements.result: 1,252 decisions (the live sessions, nine twin lanes, the development workspace), EUR 2.91; 790 verdicts and 462 unsure; harvested as silver: 239 usable (role 161, category code 32 plus 14, identifier 32), 418 self-judged and kept apart, 133 not usable (never measured or below 0.8)
measurements.against_gate: Not scored: real decisions have no truth; their silver weight comes from the homework measurement.
limits: Conversation points were never measured, so their verdicts are kept but not usable.

measurements.name: Claude's review of the 50 past experiments
measurements.gate: none fixed: a second reviewer beside the campaign's
measurements.result: 50 reviewed, 49 parsed (one cut by its length, kept raw), EUR 3.03; 184 challenges to claims (64 high, 98 medium, 22 low) against 76 by the earlier reviewer on the same experiments
measurements.against_gate: Not scored: challenges are advisory until critic_gate checks them against the recomputed numbers.

outcome: Claude has judged every past decision and reviewed every past experiment; its reliability is measured where the truth is known, its verdicts on real work are silver with honest weights, and every judgment is kept whole and archived.
lessons: Measure a judge where the truth is known before using its verdicts where it is not.
A model's stated confidence can be the best weight: here its high-confidence verdicts never failed.
Keep the whole reply before any field that must be short.
risks: The silver weights follow the latest judge run; a new run changes them.
